rfc0018_reference_digests.note: Recorded for continuity only. This challenge did not edit RFC0018 or its signed plan.

challenge_summary: The RFC is the smallest complete design for the maintainer-selected single final audio marker: it reuses the existing audio oneof plus completed flag, keeps playback_sequence wire fields unused for compatibility, and moves success admission to message lifecycle after producer, synthesis, and transport evidence. The local code confirms each high-risk surface called out by the RFC and plan: current lifecycle receipt admission is too weak, streamers still admit payload-less terminals, transports still carry sequence identity, producers can emit intermediate done signals, and TTS/watchdog boundaries can be mistaken for final synthesis. No blocking or major design findings were found; implementation still requires the exact-digest maintainer confirmation gate before code changes.

findings.title: No blocking challenge findings against the final RFC bytes
findings.details: The RFC and plan cover the requested audio completed=true marker, producer/tool finality, provider flush versus final synthesis, explicit audio oneof admission, duplicate/stale/late output, pause/flush/error handling, callback-during-Send, text-only behavior, and compatibility of retained unused sequence fields.

code_evidence.observation: The candidate states one final audio marker per message ID, no sequence tracking, explicit audio oneof only, text-only independence, failure handling, retained unused sequence fields, and required tests.
The plan acceptance criteria match the RFC contract, keeps protos and RFC0018 out of scope, and lists the exact risk areas that must be verified.

Text completion is currently emitted separately, audio end sends an explicit empty audio completed marker, and receipt handling currently records a diagnostic playback event only. This supports the RFC's division between text completion, marker issuance, and lifecycle-owned success.

Current receipt admission only checks active context, terminal-issued, and duplicate state. The RFC correctly requires expanding lifecycle ownership to generation closure, synthesis end, interruption state, send outcome, and one terminal result.
Assistant text completion currently emits assistant_turn=complete. The RFC explicitly prevents generation end alone from completing audio messages while preserving the text-only path.
Session lifecycle already owns idle timer start and expiry validation through MessageLifecycle.CanStartIdleTimeout, matching the RFC's owner split.
Playback receipts are synchronously dispatched and currently carry id plus playback_sequence. RFC0019 can ignore the sequence field while retaining the wire data.
Plain gRPC currently treats a completed message with nil oneof as an audio terminal. The RFC and plan explicitly require text and payload-less completion not to close audio playback.
WebRTC output routing currently accepts either audio oneof or nil oneof plus completed as audio. The RFC's audio-oneof-only rule covers this required change.
WebRTC drains resampler/codec tail before local playback receipt and currently carries playback_sequence. The RFC keeps the drain behavior but removes sequence identity from completion admission.

Telephony media currently keys queued responses by id plus playback_sequence, emits receipts after output drain, and marks failed writes. RFC0019's single message-level marker requires simplifying identity while preserving failure and drain behavior.
Asterisk AudioSocket currently admits nil oneof plus completed. This is explicitly covered by the audio-only final marker requirement.
Model completion currently executes tool calls before emitting LLMResponseDonePacket. The RFC correctly makes the outer response executor responsible for final closure after admitted continuations.
AgentKit has an independent completed-text boundary, so including all producer lanes in the plan is necessary.
The websocket LLM path has a separate complete response translation, confirming the plan must cover websocket producer finality.
Agentflow can emit done packets at node boundaries, matching the RFC's warning that workflow node completion is not automatically whole-message finality.
Cartesia emits TextToSpeechEndPacket only after provider flush completion, so the RFC's provider-flush versus final-synthesis distinction is required and code-grounded.
Rime has the same provider confirmed flush boundary, which the RFC includes.
The watchdog can emit TextToSpeechEndPacket on deadline expiry. The RFC explicitly says timeout is failure, not successful completion, so implementation must change this path accordingly.
Local protobuf sources already retain playback_sequence fields at their RFC0018 tags. RFC0019 correctly leaves protos out of scope and requires those fields to remain unused and unchanged.

negative_checks: Did not edit RFC0018 or its signed plan.
Did not remove or reuse playback_sequence wire fields.
remaining_work: Maintainer must approve the exact digest 052a55f717d3134d6c33c0ca9035d0c7f82e98d3e06092c06e6b2fe1aef4f1de before implementation starts.

Implementation must update every allowed producer, synthesis, lifecycle, adapter, and transport path together and run the plan's focused tests plus just agent-finalize with the exact changed-file inventory.
Callback authority should remain disabled or diagnostic-only for unverified clients until native, gRPC, and WebRTC behavior is verified against the audio-only marker contract.
